newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday November 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday November 22.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Tension seems to be easing between majority parties and the opposition as the 1997 budget enters the Upper House for examination. Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi threatens "tax obstructionism" but some centre-right members would like to reopen political dialogue with the ruling coalition. Leftist PDS party Senate leader Cesare Salvi says the government is ready to discuss the Eurotax and the highly controversial special powers it has asked for (all).
* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro in a letter to the parliament said state-television RAI should be more objective. RAI is accused of favouring the ruling coalition (all).

* The government approved a reform presented by Justice Minister Giovanni Maria Flick, including measures for a more restrictive use of wire-tappings. Under the plan, magistrates will be regularly judged by the Superior Council of Magistrates (CSM). After two negative evaluations they might be suspended from their functions (Corriere della Sera).
* Italian police raided homes of supporters of the separatist Northern League in connection with a probe into the alleged formation of a military organisation (all).
* After November CPI from six sample cities, analysts forecast a 2.6 percent rise in inflation year on year. It is the lowest level since June 1969 (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi confirmed the government intends to bring the lira back into the ERM by the end of November (all).
* The government decided with a decree law that telecoms holding STET would pass with immediate effect from the hands of state industrial holding group IRI to the Treasury (all).
* Electricity group ENEL will reorganise its business into three main operating divisions -- production, transmission and distribution (all).

* In an interview, Monaco-based businessman Luigi Giribaldi, who has raised its stake up to 20 percent in Carlo De Benedetti financial holding Cofide, says he has contacts with De Benedetti but he is following an independent strategy (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
